summary: Tested salary extraction feature. Fixed a regex bug where em-dash (—) character was not included in salary range patterns, causing only max values to be extracted instead of full ranges. All 5 backend tests pass. Frontend extraction utility now correctly parses $X CAD, $X-$Y ranges, $XK notation, and displays 'Salary not listed' when appropriate.
critical_code_review_comments: extractSalary.js correctly handles CAD/USD/EUR/GBP currencies with appropriate symbols (CA$, €, £, A$)
Salary ranges now properly extracted with em-dash (—), en-dash (–), and hyphen (-) separators
getDisplaySalary() correctly prioritizes: 1) structured salary_min/max fields, 2) salary text field, 3) description extraction
Dashboard.jsx and JobSearch.jsx both apply text-emerald-400 class for extracted salaries
Sanity checks prevent false positives: hourly < $500, annual >= $10K and < $10M

success_rate.frontend: Code review passed - extraction utility verified via Node.js tests

seed_data_creation: None - used existing saved jobs data
context_for_next_testing_agent: Salary extraction feature is implemented and tested. The extractSalary.js utility at /app/frontend/src/utils/extractSalary.js handles various salary patterns. Bug was fixed where em-dash (—) character in job descriptions (common in Airbnb jobs) was not being recognized as a range separator. Dashboard saved jobs section displays extracted salaries in emerald green. Auth uses Emergent Google Auth with session cookies.

features_tested.Structured salary precedence: PASS - Uses salary_min/max fields when available
features_tested.Salary not listed fallback: PASS - Shows when no salary found
features_tested.Emerald green styling: PASS - text-emerald-400 applied in Dashboard.jsx and JobSearch.jsx

bug_fixes_applied.issue: Em-dash (—) not recognized in salary range patterns
bug_fixes_applied.root_cause: Regex pattern (?:-|to|–) only included hyphen, 'to', and en-dash but not em-dash
bug_fixes_applied.fix_applied: Updated regex to use (?:[-–—]|to) to include all dash characters
